verdict: Meta's revenue rose 22% to $39.1B as ad impressions and prices both climbed 10% — and even with a $1.4B Texas legal settlement in its costs, it kept $13.5B as profit, about 34 cents of every dollar.

kpis.label: Family DAP
kpis.note: people using a Meta app daily, +7%

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — ad impressions rose 10% and the average price per ad rose 10%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: Mostly WhatsApp business messaging and other fees from the social apps.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and Ray-Ban Meta glasses — $353M of revenue against a $4.5B operating loss.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers building the apps, the AI models and the headsets.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and devices, and promoting the apps.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Legal, finance and overhead for running the company — this quarter it includes a $1.4B legal settlement charge.

otherDetail: Interest and other income of $259M, net.
follow100Note: Advertising alone is $98.10 of every $100 Meta takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Ads did the lifting
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue grew 22% to $38.3B — 98 cents of every dollar Meta made — helped by 10% more ad views and a 10% higher average price per ad.

takeaways.title: Reality Labs still burns cash
takeaways.text: Reality Labs lost $4.5B in the quarter on just $353M of revenue, and Meta said it expects the segment's operating losses to keep growing as it builds headsets and glasses.

takeaways.title: Cash generation stayed enormous
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $10.9B even after $8.5B of capital spending, and Meta raised its full-year capex outlook to $37–40B, mostly for AI computing.

oneTimers: A $1.4B charge for Meta's settlement with the State of Texas (over its past use of facial-recognition data) sits inside general & administrative costs. Without it, operating income would have been about $16.2B instead of $14.8B.
